messages.subject: Count data and occupancy
parts:
Hi All,

I am running a multiple season single species occupancy analysis on 3 years of bat data. I used a stratified random sampling design; 5 regions/strata with 9 randomly selected sampling sites within each region, for a total of 45 sampling sites. Each site was sampled for a 7 night period 4 times each year (corresponding to bat reproductive cycles) during the 3 year study. This provided 84 discrete observations for each of the 45 sampling sites (7x4x3 = 84).


I also have a detector in each of the 5 regions that has been collecting nightly activity data every night for the past 4 years and I'm wondering if I can use the data in any way in the occupancy models. I know 5 sites is a small number but with so many replicates I wonder if something can be done with the data other than a separate activity study. The results are showing that all of my sites are occupied, so it looks like I didn't collect the right data to model any changes in occupancy, however I still want to know what is driving detection probability, colonization, and extinction. It has been mentioned that perhaps abundance data or count data could be used to give you more information about detection probabilities but I'm not sure what type of analysis this is or if it would work in my situation. Any thoughts/ideas on this method would be greatly appreciated. Thanks so much to all of the unmarked users who have helped thus far!

Cheers,

Rachel
